records.title: Outer-Pedal Area Products in Elliptic Billiards
records.description:
For a fixed confocal elliptic-caustic billiard family with least period congruent to two modulo four, we prove that the signed area of the outer tangent polygon times the signed area of its pedal polygon with respect to any fixed point is constant. Coprime star trajectories are included. The outer polygon is an explicit affine image of a half-step shift of the billiard orbit. After complexification, its area and the outer-pedal area have disjoint possible simple-pole sets. Central pairing separates the pedal map into two area traces, and two reversal symmetries provide the complementary zeros that make the product entire and elliptic. This establishes invariant k303,a under an explicitly stated least-period convention.

Source record: AMR-050-0014 (raw ID 5100014, k303,a), Hugging Face dataset ulamai/UnsolvedMath. The arbitrary-point dependence is radial quadratic. For the six-periodic family with lambda=a^2*b^2/(a+b)^2, the invariant equals a*b*(a+2*b)*(2*a+b)*(1+|M|^2/(a+b)^2). Exact standard-library polynomial and quadratic-field controls verify the formulas and actual geometry. Two same-caustic triangles, each traversed twice, give a counterexample to the unrestricted six-entry-list interpretation; they do not refute the genuine least-period theorem. Hyperbolic and degenerate caustics are excluded. This is a self-audited, AI-assisted, unrefereed preprint, not an independently human-reviewed or formally verified proof. Prior confocal geometry, canonical Jacobi parametrization, adjacent tangent-pedal results and the established complex-pole method are credited. No first-proof or absolute priority claim is made.

records.title: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards
records.description:
For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the primitive least period is congruent to 2 modulo 4. The result covers all admissible primitive star turns and both orientations. For every even least period, the two focal products are equal at each phase. Repetitions raise the positive primitive product to an integer power, so listed return length alone is insufficient. Circles are treated separately; hyperbolic and degenerate caustics are excluded.

This research note proves the primitive interpretation of the experimentally recorded invariant k114 in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller (2020/2021), establishes the exact period classification, and gives an exact doubled-triangle counterexample to the unrestricted six-event return interpretation. It applies Stachel's published parametrization, classical Jacobi identities and established meromorphic divisor methods. No new-method or exclusive historical priority claim is made. The bounded primary-source audit found no explicit earlier proof of this exact target; novelty of the specific formulation is not certified. Full text of one related 2023 Dragović–Gajić article was unavailable, and the accompanying priority note records that coverage gap.

The deposit contains the manuscript PDF and a support archive with standalone LaTeX source, exact finite arithmetic controls, independent supplementary theta-series diagnostics, recorded outputs, metadata, references and priority-search limits. records.title: Pedal Areas of Periodic Elliptic Billiard Trajectories with Respect to an Arbitrary Point
records.description:
Reznik, Garcia and Koiller listed many quantities that are experimentally constant along the families of N-periodic billiard trajectories in an ellipse whose caustic is a confocal ellipse. We treat three of their rows on the signed areas of pedal polygons with respect to an arbitrary point M. Let A be the signed area of the trajectory, A′ that of its outer polygon, and A_M, A′_M the signed areas of their pedal polygons with respect to M. The rows state that A·A_M is constant for N ≡ 0 (mod 4) (row k203,a), A/A_M for N ≡ 2 (mod 4) (row k204) and A′/A′_M for N ≡ 0 (mod 4) (row k304). We prove them for trajectories of least period N, every winding number and every point M, real or complex (the two ratios wherever they are defined). For k203,a we use a Jacobi parametrisation of the family, in which the product is an elliptic function of the phase. Its possible poles lie at the poles of the vertices and at the points where a side normal is isotropic; these two sets are disjoint exactly when N is odd or divisible by 4, an order-reversing symmetry makes each factor vanish at the poles of the other, and Liouville's theorem concludes. For N ≡ 2 (mod 4) we prove A_M = κ(M)A, and for the outer polygon with N ≡ 0 (mod 4) we prove A′_M = κ′(M)A′, where κ and κ′ are quadratic in M with positive constant terms. So the ratios are constant wherever κ(M) ≠ 0, resp. κ′(M) ≠ 0; the exceptional set can be a real circle in star families (an exact example with N = 8 for the outer polygon). For even N the part of A_M that is linear in M vanishes. The rows are due to Reznik, Garcia and Koiller, and the parametrisation is Stachel's. The case M = O of k203,a is in an earlier note of the author, and the dependence of A′_M on M for every even N was proved by Kriebel; for k304 only the constancy of A′/A′_O for N ≡ 0 (mod 4) is new. This is an unrefereed note.

Unrefereed preprint released for independent mathematical scrutiny. Publication on Zenodo does not constitute peer review. AI-assisted tools supported research, computation, proof development, and manuscript preparation. The author remains responsible for all claims and the final text.

Corpus identifiers: AMR-050-0011, AMR-050-0013, AMR-050-0016 (Reznik–Garcia–Koiller, Eighty new invariants of N-periodics in the elliptic billiard, arXiv:2004.12497v11, rows k203,a, k204 and k304; journal version Arnold Math. J. 7 (2021)).

records.title: Global Hessian realizations of statistical manifolds
records.description:
Every smooth Hausdorff second-countable statistical manifold of fixed finite dimension n at least 1, without boundary and with positive-definite metric, admits a proper global statistical embedding into an open subset of R^N with one smooth positive Hessian potential, where N=binomial(2n+4,3). Orthogonal projection of the standard flat connection and its metric dual induces the prescribed ordered pair of torsion-free dual connections. For a general mutually dual pair, both torsions vanishing is necessary and sufficient for realization by a torsion-free dually flat ambient manifold. Countable zero-dimensional inputs are treated separately. The ambient neighborhood may be nonconvex and incomplete; dual affine coordinates are local. No finite-probability-model, global-gradient-injectivity or optimal-dimension conclusion is asserted.

The construction answers the historical realization question in item1(a) of Furuhata, Matsuzoe and Urakawa, Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics (1998), in the stated smooth positive boundaryless scope. A proper Whitney embedding followed by all polynomial features through degree three gives a fixed finite scalar-jet spanning family. A smooth fiberwise right inverse produces an exact global Lauritzen pair, including the prescribed cubic and connection signs. A normal-neighborhood extension and a nonuniform Schur-complement penalty give one positive Hessian potential on a neighborhood of the entire embedded manifold, without compactness or uniform geometric bounds.

This is a fully credited self-contained construction note. Lauritzen, Matumoto, Le, the Nash/Gromov free-map lineage, Marugame, Whitney and tubular-neighborhood theory provide substantial ancestry; Osipov gives genuine global special-curvature predecessors. Early unrestricted finite-simplex claims are disclosed. Actual Ay-Jost-Le-Schwachhofer2017 Theorems4.10 and4.11 distinguish finite models for compact inputs from countable models for noncompact inputs. Bounded independent primary-source priority audits did not establish a verified unrestricted predecessor, but material final-body access gaps remain. records.title: Three anti-invariant classes on a nonintegrable four-manifold
records.description:
We construct smooth nonintegrable almost complex structures on the closed real four-manifold given by a genus-two curve times an elliptic curve, with at least three independent real closed anti-invariant de Rham classes. The structures equal the product complex structure outside one coordinate ball and converge to it in the smooth topology. This gives a negative answer to the unrestricted Draghici-Li-Zhang integrability conjecture. No exact value of the anti-invariant dimension, compatibility with a fixed symplectic form or real analyticity is asserted.

The complete proof uses two holomorphic two-forms on the product, a Stokes argument for three real cohomology classes, and a compactly supported exact deformation preserving a variable-coefficient relation among their representatives. A positive real two-plane defines the new almost complex structure; an explicit differential of a complex coframe proves nonintegrability. The earlier generic-vanishing theorem is credited to all four authors Tan, Wang, Zhang and Zhu. Li-Zhang and Draghici-Li-Zhang cohomology, Donaldson positive planes, Bande-Kotschick closed pairs, Hind-Tomassini examples and Chen-Zhang nonintegrable products provide material prior context.

records.title: A type-D4 counterexample to the canonical-potential exponent converse
records.description:
The exponent-bound converse stated for canonical GHKK potentials in Schumann's 2021 Oberwolfach report is false. For an explicit reduced word in type D4, the canonical potential has 22 combined monomials, all of coefficient one, and all 22 inequalities define distinct facets, although two monomials have exponent minus two in one canonical coordinate. The reduced word and its complete string-coordinate support occur in earlier public computations; we extract the consequence for the historical formulation and supply an independent canonical calculation and exact integer certificates. The chamber-ansatz pullback has all exponents in {-1,0,1}, so the later string-coordinate converse is not refuted. No first-priority or current-openness claim is made.

Extensively AI-assisted, unrefereed corrective and verification note. No external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification. The reduced word and complete transformed support occur in Denis Mironov's older public crystal data, Case 267; no first discovery, first resolution, or current-openness claim is made. The deposit includes the five-page note and a portable source and exact-verification archive. The later string-coordinate and coefficient conjectures are not refuted.

records.title: Negative answers to the printed totally mixed face questions
records.description:

Its rational Betti numbers are (2,22,0,...), so it is nonshellable and fails the printed sphere-wedge homology assertion. The shared interval factor deliberately gives a nongeneric example.

records.title: A negative answer to Nevo's homology-sphere decomposition question
records.description:
A finite pure two-dimensional abstract simplicial complex is constructed which is doubly Cohen-Macaulay over every characteristic-zero field but contains no two-dimensional homology-sphere subcomplex over any field. This gives a full negative answer to Nevo's sphere replacement question, OWR17/2005 Problem8 (printed961) and Discrete and Computational Geometry39(2008) Problem3.7 (printed417). Homology sphere includes all face-link conditions, not merely global sphere homology. No subdivision or enlargement is used.

The construction is a finite congruence quotient of the affine PGL3 building over F11((y)). A faithful polynomial representation and reduction modulo t^9 give sufficient displacement and unchanged projective-plane links. A direct deleted-link spectral estimate and a complete weighted cocycle proof verify every vertex deletion. An Euler characteristic count excludes all permitted sphere pieces. The earlier building and representation of Lubotzky-Samuels-Vishne, degree/congruence mechanism of Lubotzky-Meshulam, Garland-type criterion of Ballmann-Swiatkowski, and curvature obstruction of Januszkiewicz-Swiatkowski receive explicit credit.

records.title: A fixed birational map without a prime-field cycle-distribution limit
records.description:
For the fixed birational map L(u,v)=(u,(u²+1)v), every prime p congruent to 3 modulo 4 gives a permutation of the full affine plane F_p². With point-weighted periods normalized by p, the distribution function at every fixed 1/2≤x<1 equals 1−φ(p−1)/(p−1)+o(1), has limsup 1 and liminf at most 23/24. Neither these CDF values nor the period probability measures converge on any further admissible prime subset of positive upper relative density.

A separate proposition covers every odd prime on the invariant regular domain of size p(p-r), where r is zero or two. The primitive principal term is (p-r)φ(p−1)/(p−1). Under uniform-point deletion or arbitrary finite nonnegative assigned periods only on exceptional fibers, bounded statistics change by O(1/p). The regular CDF and a globally bounded continuous ramp thus exclude convergence on every positive-upper-prime-density selection under these conventions. Completed measures are on nonnegative reals; assigned periods may exceed p. Primes congruent to 1 modulo 4 still do not give full-affine permutations.

This is a precisely scoped application to the broad existence assertion in Vivaldi's 2004 Oberwolfach contribution, joint work with Roberts. The triangular family, quadratic primitive-value machinery, shifted-prime totient mean and continuous scalar empirical law are established and credited to the actual sources. The positive-density selection conclusion uses the old atomless scalar law, not merely the existence of two subsequences. No new map family, character-sum theorem, arithmetic mean, scalar law, universal elliptic theorem, polynomial-automorphism theorem or prime-average cycle theorem is claimed.

The bounded priority audit authenticated no earlier statement of this exact application in the inspected sources. The cited Neumärker–Roberts–Viallet–Vivaldi 2011 preprint body and version relationships remain unrecovered; no inference about its unseen contents is made. No worldwide novelty, current-open status or historical firstness is claimed.

The source/verification ZIP preserves all 17 original research files and historical mathematical audit artifacts, supplies exact manifests and a new dependency-free standard-library checker. The latter passed 147,619 finite exact checks over 87 admissible primes through 1000, eight full affine orbit graphs with 6,088 points, six bad-reduction controls and a totient bound through 10,000. An additional separate checker passes 46,298 exact controls over all 167 odd primes through 1000 (80 class1,87 class3), including 10,178 raw regular graph points and exceptional assignments beyond p. Historical 8,347,742 finite assertions and 230,780 analytic controls are separate retained runs. Original SymPy scripts were not successfully replayed in this preparation; the analytic proof and explicitly cited classical inputs establish the infinite-prime statements.
